name: 1064 Western Road
summary: This 1870 Gothic Revival house has pale lap siding, dark steep side gables and a road-facing central cross gable with a narrow pointed upper window. A pitched open entrance porch has a timber balustrade.

parts.name: Open porch gable above the entrance
Central pointed cross gable above the road-facing porch

lidarNote: Regional-2m LiDAR gives a P50 of 10.54 m, P90 of 14.62 m, and maximum of 16.1 m, which overstate the house height because the tallest returns fall on the wooded east side and tree canopy makes upper quantiles unreliable. The street photograph shows one full storey and one upper storey under the roof, with eaves about 4.8 m and main ridge about 8.6 m estimated from door and sash proportions.

evidence.note: Two upright sash windows sit side by side in the upper southeast gable at 1064 Western Road, framed by pale horizontal siding and dark shingles.
The central pointed sash has an arched head, pierced bargeboard and a smaller gabled front porch below.
A single recessed door sits behind wood posts, a rail and paired pitched roof planes.

Dark gable roof immediately beside Western Road with the rear half under mature trees, with the dark roof colour sampled in the street frame 148668931 at (73.1%, 55.5%) measuring #262b33 instead of the aerial image.

Regional-2m LiDAR gives a P50 of 10.54 m, P90 of 14.62 m, and maximum of 16.1 m, which overstate the house height because the tallest returns fall on the wooded east side and tree canopy makes upper quantiles unreliable. House material samples in frame 148668931 measure pale siding at (71.6%, 66%) as #c5c0bf and the dark roof at (73.1%, 55.5%) as #262b33.

Frames 148668931 and 136745489 show a central cross gable rising from the road-facing eave above a smaller pitched porch, with one central pointed sash and two upstairs side-by-side single-hung sashes on the southeast gable.

notes: The rear lean-to is partly under tree cover. Its depth follows the mapped back wall; door and window positions there are estimates. Street photographs show sawn bargeboards and turned porch balusters.
